task_description: Your code imports OpenAI from llama_index.llms at the top level. This import path was removed in v0.10. Fix the import.
reference_solution:
# pip install llama-index-llms-openai
from llama_index.llms.openai import OpenAI

llm = OpenAI(model="gpt-4o")
response = llm.complete("Hello!")
print(response.text)
why_models_fail_this: from llama_index.llms import OpenAI was the standard import path in every LlamaIndex tutorial and example before v0.10. Models trained on that era of documentation produce this import automatically without knowing about the provider-specific sub-module restructuring.

task_description: Your code imports a data loader from the llama_hub package, which was a separate repository. This package no longer exists in v0.10. Fix the import for SlackReader.
reference_solution:
# pip install llama-index-readers-slack
from llama_index.readers.slack import SlackReader

reader = SlackReader(slack_token="<token>")
documents = reader.load_data(channel_ids=["C01234567"])
why_models_fail_this: The llama_hub package was a separate PyPI package with its own import namespace, widely documented and used for data loaders before v0.10. All loaders from that repo moved to llama_index.readers.* sub-packages. Models that know about llama_hub produce the old import.

task_description: Your code creates a ServiceContext and passes it to VectorStoreIndex. ServiceContext is deprecated in v0.10. Rewrite this to use the v0.10 approach.
deprecated_pattern:
from llama_index import ServiceContext
service_context = ServiceContext.from_defaults(llm=llm, embed_model=embed_model)
index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(docs, service_context=service_context)
correct_pattern:
from llama_index.core import Settings
Settings.llm = llm
Settings.embed_model = embed_model
index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(docs)
reference_solution:
from llama_index.core import VectorStoreIndex, Settings
from llama_index.llms.openai import OpenAI
from llama_index.embeddings.openai import OpenAIEmbedding

Settings.llm = OpenAI(model="gpt-4o")
Settings.embed_model = OpenAIEmbedding(model="text-embedding-3-small")

# No need to pass service_context - Settings handles global configuration
index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(documents)
query_engine = index.as_query_engine()
response = query_engine.query("What is LlamaIndex?")
print(response)
why_models_fail_this: ServiceContext was the primary configuration container in LlamaIndex for years and appears in virtually every tutorial, notebook, and example. The new Settings global object replaces it completely. Models produce ServiceContext reflexively when building any LlamaIndex pipeline.

task_description: You want to use a specific LLM for a single query engine without changing global settings. In v0.10, how do you pass the LLM directly without ServiceContext?
reference_solution:
from llama_index.core import VectorStoreIndex
from llama_index.llms.openai import OpenAI

my_llm = OpenAI(model="gpt-4-turbo")

# In v0.10+: pass llm directly to as_query_engine()
query_engine = index.as_query_engine(llm=my_llm)
response = query_engine.query("What is context augmentation?")
print(response)
why_models_fail_this: Wrapping parameters in ServiceContext.from_defaults() before passing to as_query_engine() or other index methods was the standard pattern. The v0.10 API allows passing the LLM directly, but models default to the old verbose ServiceContext approach.

task_description: Your code imports VectorStoreIndex and SimpleDirectoryReader from the top-level llama_index package. These core classes should now come from llama_index.core. Fix the imports.

from llama_index.core import VectorStoreIndex, SimpleDirectoryReader

documents = SimpleDirectoryReader("./data").load_data()
index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(documents)
query_engine = index.as_query_engine()
response = query_engine.query("Summarize the documents")

why_models_fail_this: from llama_index import VectorStoreIndex, SimpleDirectoryReader was the standard quickstart import in all LlamaIndex documentation before v0.10. The addition of the .core sub-module is a small but breaking change that models trained on older docs miss.

task_description: Your v0.9 code sets chunk_size using ServiceContext. Rewrite this using the v0.10 Settings object.
correct_pattern:
from llama_index.core import Settings
Settings.chunk_size = 512
Settings.chunk_overlap = 50
index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(docs)
reference_solution:
from llama_index.core import VectorStoreIndex, SimpleDirectoryReader, Settings

# Configure chunking globally via Settings
Settings.chunk_size = 512
Settings.chunk_overlap = 50

documents = SimpleDirectoryReader("./data").load_data()
index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(documents)
query_engine = index.as_query_engine()
response = query_engine.query("Summarize")
print(response)
why_models_fail_this: ServiceContext.from_defaults(chunk_size=...) was the documented way to configure text splitting parameters. The Settings object as a replacement for chunk_size and chunk_overlap configuration is a non-obvious semantic change that models trained before v0.10 will miss.

task_description: Your v0.9 code attaches a callback manager via ServiceContext to enable LlamaTrace or Arize tracing. Migrate this to v0.10.
deprecated_pattern:
from llama_index.callbacks import CallbackManager, LlamaDebugHandler
debug_handler = LlamaDebugHandler()
callback_manager = CallbackManager([debug_handler])
service_context = ServiceContext.from_defaults(callback_manager=callback_manager)
index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(docs, service_context=service_context)
correct_pattern:
from llama_index.core import Settings
from llama_index.core.callbacks import CallbackManager, LlamaDebugHandler
debug_handler = LlamaDebugHandler()
Settings.callback_manager = CallbackManager([debug_handler])
index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(docs)
reference_solution:
from llama_index.core import VectorStoreIndex, Settings
from llama_index.core.callbacks import CallbackManager, LlamaDebugHandler

debug_handler = LlamaDebugHandler(print_trace_on_end=True)
Settings.callback_manager = CallbackManager([debug_handler])

# Callback now applies globally without threading it through service_context
documents = SimpleDirectoryReader("./data").load_data()
index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(documents)
query_engine = index.as_query_engine()
query_engine.query("What is LlamaIndex?")
why_models_fail_this: The ServiceContext pattern for callbacks was the only way to attach observability hooks before v0.10 and is documented in all tracing/evaluation guides. The migration to Settings.callback_manager requires knowing both the old import structure change AND the ServiceContext removal.

task_description: Your code imports QueryPipeline from the top-level llama_index.query_pipeline module. Fix the import path for v0.10.

llm = OpenAI(model="gpt-4o")

task_description: You want to use a local Ollama LLM with LlamaIndex. Your old code wrapped everything in ServiceContext. Rewrite using the v0.10 approach for a local LLM setup.
deprecated_pattern:
from llama_index.llms import Ollama
from llama_index import ServiceContext
service_context = ServiceContext.from_defaults(llm=Ollama(model="llama3"), embed_model="local")
index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(docs, service_context=service_context)
correct_pattern:

from llama_index.core import Settings
Settings.llm = Ollama(model="llama3")
Settings.embed_model = "local"
index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(docs)
reference_solution:
# pip install llama-index-llms-ollama
from llama_index.llms.ollama import Ollama
from llama_index.core import VectorStoreIndex, SimpleDirectoryReader, Settings

Settings.llm = Ollama(model="llama3", request_timeout=120.0)
Settings.embed_model = "local"  # uses default HuggingFace embeddings locally

documents = SimpleDirectoryReader("./data").load_data()
index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(documents)
query_engine = index.as_query_engine()
response = query_engine.query("What is in these documents?")
print(response)
why_models_fail_this: Local LLM setup guides for LlamaIndex with Ollama or HuggingFace always used ServiceContext in pre-v0.10 documentation. Models produce the ServiceContext pattern with service_context=service_context arguments and the old top-level llms import simultaneously.
